description: A founder's PR/FAQ v0 assumption list for one idea. Synthetic, written for these evals.

input.idea: An app that chases missing receipts for small bookkeeping firms, 49 euros a seat per month.

assumptions.a2: At least 6 of 10 bookkeepers we interview at firms of 2-10 people lost 3 or more hours last month chasing client receipts.
assumptions.a3: At least 3 of 10 firm owners who see the price agree to a paid pilot at 49 euros a seat.
assumptions.a4: Clients prefer a text message link to email.
assumptions.a5: The market for bookkeeping software is huge.

items.note: Only a2 and a3 name who, a number and a threshold. Paying is what sinks the business; the reminder channel costs an afternoon.

input.idea: A booking page for independent dog groomers that takes a deposit to stop no-shows.

assumptions.b1: Groomers we reach in two Facebook groups lose at least 2 appointments a week to no-shows.
assumptions.b2: Dog owners will accept paying a 10 euro deposit: fewer than 1 in 5 abandon the booking at the deposit step in a 50-booking test.
assumptions.b4: At least 5 of 20 groomers we contact already use some deposit or card-on-file method.

items.note: If owners walk away at the deposit, the product removes bookings instead of saving them.

input.idea: A shared repair log for landlords with two to ten flats, 9 euros per flat per month.

assumptions.c1: Landlords want to be more organised.
assumptions.c2: At least half of 12 landlords we interview had a repair request go unanswered for 48 hours or more in the last six months.
assumptions.c3: Tenants will report repairs in the app rather than by WhatsApp: at least 60 percent of requests in a 4-week pilot come through the app.
assumptions.c4: Landlords with 2-10 flats will pay 9 euros per flat: 4 of 12 agree to pay for a 3-month pilot.

items.note: c3 matters, but a workaround exists (the landlord logs requests); nobody paying ends the business.

input.idea: Automatic stock reorder for food trucks, paid by the collective that runs them.

assumptions.d1: Collectives, not individual truck owners, control the budget for stock tools: in 8 of 10 collectives we call, one person approves spending over 100 euros a month.
assumptions.d2: Trucks often run out of things.
assumptions.d4: Owners would probably like fewer stock-outs.
assumptions.d5: Suppliers will accept orders by API or email within 12 hours: at least 3 of the 5 largest suppliers in Lisbon confirm.

items.note: d2 names no who and no threshold of trucks; the buyer being the collective is the load-bearing claim for a product it pays for.

input.idea: A price-rise clause generator for kitchen renovators.

assumptions.e2: At least 7 of 15 renovators we interview absorbed a material price rise of 5 percent or more on a job in the last year.
assumptions.e3: Clients will sign a quote with a price-validity clause as often as without one: acceptance within 5 points across 40 quotes.
assumptions.e4: Renovators will pay 15 euros a month for the generator: 5 of 15 prepay a month.

items.note: If clients refuse quotes with the clause, renovators lose jobs by using it, and no price makes that worth paying for.
